A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoordTok research and contain 15 readable pages, including Appendices A–E. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original UCF-101 video reconstruction, generation, efficiency, and ablation results in Section 3, with additional results in Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the CoordTok reconstruction and generation evaluations and supplementary results.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix A retain the same triplane encoder, coordinate sampling and interpolation, transformer decoder, two-stage reconstruction training, and SiT generation procedure. Figure 2's revisions are graphical.

E1.justification: Both versions use UCF-101 for video tokenization, reconstruction, and unconditional generation, with the same video-length scenarios. No dataset, domain, or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The respective comparator sets in Tables 1–3 and the empirical figures are unchanged, including the tokenization comparisons with LARP and PVDM-AE and generation comparisons with PVDM-L and HVDM. Appendix C's baseline descriptions also match.

E3.justification: The preprocessing, model configurations, training budgets, sampling procedures, and metrics match. Both retain 10000 reconstruction clips and 2048 clips for generation FVD evaluation, as documented in Section 3 and Appendices A–B.

E4.justification: The model-size, triplane-size, sampling, dynamics, and frequency analyses in Section 3.4 are unchanged. The token-count comparison and supplementary qualitative examples are also retained without new analyses.

E5.justification: The tables retain the same point-estimate reporting and Figure 8 retains the same Pearson correlations. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or statistical-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative examples match. For example, both report CoordTok PSNR 28.6 in Table 1, generation FVD 369.3 in Table 2, and rFVD 102.9 versus 100.5 for 1280 versus 3072 tokens in Appendix Table 8.

T1.justification: The coordinate and patch definitions, bilinear-interpolation equations (1–2), and dynamics-magnitude formula (3) are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient long-video tokenization, reduced token counts, and memory-efficient generation of 128 frames at once.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations for token-count effects and reconstruction behavior. The difficulty with dynamic videos and proposed future use of multiple or adaptive content planes remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The architecture tables, hyperparameters, preprocessing instructions, sampler details, hardware specifications, and project-site link are unchanged. The new acknowledgement of compute support adds attribution without additional implementation or resource-access instructions.

R1.justification: The same 68 cited works and the same research positioning in Section 4 are retained. Bibliography reflow and an updated citation backreference do not change the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 corrects 'Coordinated-based' to 'Coordinate-based' in the main and supplementary titles, adjusts affiliation spacing, and adds acknowledgements covering funding, NVIDIA compute support, and an author's concurrent appointment. The scientific narrative and section organization otherwise match.

P2.justification: Figure 2 receives small typography and spacing revisions, including the output-coordinate label, while retaining its components and dimensions. There is limited text and bibliography reflow; no empirical figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The corrected title and more consistent Figure 2 typography provide modest editorial polish. The new acknowledgements improve transparency about funding, compute support, and institutional involvement. These are limited gains; the methods, empirical evidence, and stated limitations remain unchanged.
